assumedContext: Network egress blocked except the search index; filing figures reached this analysis via search-index summaries.
Meta discloses no AI-attributable revenue line. All revenue-per-gigawatt statements are inferences from consolidated figures, not measurements.
FY2026 revenue of ~$252bn is an analyst estimate built from reported Q1 ($56.31bn) and Q2 ($60.80bn), guided Q3 ($61-64bn) and an estimated Q4 (~$72bn).

findings.claim: Meta has essentially no contracted revenue: no take-or-pay, no minimum-volume floor, no indexation and no multi-year offtake stands behind roughly $240bn of annual advertising. Every dollar is re-won in a spot auction.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Structural conclusion from Meta's disclosed revenue model (Q2 2026 results and 10-Q); no contracted-revenue or RPO disclosure exists in Meta's reporting

findings.claim: Incremental operating margin for FY2026E is 3.3% against an FY2025 average operating margin of 41.4%: revenue rises about $51.0bn (to ~$252bn from $200.97bn) while operating income rises about $1.7bn (to ~$85bn from $83.28bn) on guided expenses of $165-169bn. Adding back the $2.4bn legal charge and severance lifts incremental margin only to about 11%.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from Meta FY2025 actuals and FY2026 total-expense guidance of $165-169bn given with Q2 2026 results, 2026-07-29

findings.claim: Q2 2026 free cash flow was $784m, down about 91% y/y, as $31.08bn of capex consumed roughly 98% of $31.86bn of operating cash flow. Dividends of $1,353m in the quarter exceeded free cash flow by about $569m - the dividend is being funded with borrowings.
findings.label: FACT
findings.unit: USD m quarterly free cash flow

findings.claim: FY2026E free cash flow is approximately zero (estimated range -$9bn to +$6bn): H1 2026 operating cash flow $64.09bn and capex $50.94bn gave $13.17bn of first-half FCF, against full-year capex guidance of $130-145bn.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.unit: USD m FY2026E free cash flow
findings.source: Derived from reported Q1 and Q2 2026 cash flows and FY2026 capex guidance

findings.claim: At a $165bn annual capital programme each year of spending adds roughly $53bn to the annual revenue Meta must earn simply to cover its cost of capital (4.1 GW at $12.8bn/GW), against actual annual revenue increments of about $51-53bn. At the $180bn run-rate implied by 2027-28 plans the hurdle grows about $58bn a year - faster than revenue.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.unit: USD m per year of additional required revenue
findings.source: Derived from the Phase 2 unit cost curve ($12.8bn revenue required per GW per year at $40bn/GW) and FY2026 capex guidance

findings.claim: WhatsApp paid messaging surpassed a $2.0bn annual run-rate at Q4 2025, and more than 1 million businesses used Meta Business Agents weekly in Q2 2026 after global availability on WhatsApp and Messenger; early business-AI deployments in Mexico and the Philippines generate over 1 million weekly conversations each.
findings.label: FACT
findings.unit: USD m annual run-rate, WhatsApp paid messaging
findings.source: Meta Q4 2025 commentary (Futurum summary); Meta Q2 2026 disclosure and trade press, 2026

findings.claim: Consumer AI monetisation remains pre-revenue at scale: Meta AI Plus and Premium are in test markets (Singapore, Guatemala), Vibes moved to a freemium credit model, and a Hatch agent platform with a reported $199.99/month tier and a 'Watermelon' model is described only from internal documents.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Yahoo Finance/Forkast reporting on Hatch and Watermelon, 2026; tech-insider and ALM Corp summaries of Meta AI Plus/Premium and Vibes, 2026. Classified [Unfunded Planned Project] under the Phase 3 taxonomy

findings.claim: Meta open-weighted Muse Spark 1.2 and open-sourced the Muse Glimmer on-device family, deliberately foregoing model-licensing revenue. The AI capital programme must therefore be justified entirely through advertising and first-party products - there is no licensing annuity.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: CNBC 2026-08-10 on Meta open-sourcing its most powerful model; Fox Business on the Zuckerberg superintelligence memo

findings.claim: An independent revenue bridge lands on the consensus FY2027 number of about $305bn: FY2026E ~$252bn plus roughly $24bn of price, $26bn of impressions including Threads and WhatsApp Status, $5bn of business messaging, less about $2bn of youth-safety design drag. The disagreement with the market is not about revenue but about what the revenue costs.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived bridge in Phase 3 section 3.1; consensus revenue of ~$305bn for 2027 per sell-side aggregates (tikr, stockanalysis.com), retrieved 2026-09-06

findings.claim: Reality Labs generated $431m of revenue against a $4,619m operating loss in Q2 2026, a 2% wider loss than the $4,530m of Q2 2025, while Family of Apps operating income fell 6% to $23,394m from $24,971m.
findings.label: FACT
findings.unit: USD m quarterly Reality Labs operating loss

findings.claim: The highest-value commercial structures available to a capital-intensive business are absent: no upfront customer contributions to infrastructure cost, no take-or-pay, no indexation. Only premium tiers and emerging usage-based billing (messaging, agents) are in use.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Assessment of Meta's disclosed commercial terms across advertising, messaging and subscription products, Q2 2026 results and product reporting

gaps.whyItMatters: There is no disclosed figure against which the $137bn programme can be tested. It is the highest-value missing disclosure in the company and the reason every return calculation here carries a range
gaps.resolvedBy: Meta breaking out business messaging, agents and AI subscriptions, as it once did for Reality Labs

gaps.item: Threads and WhatsApp Status advertising revenue and price per ad
gaps.whyItMatters: These are the marginal new impression supply; their realised price determines whether new inventory is accretive or dilutive to the blended price per ad

gaps.item: Meta AI subscription funnel: subscribers, ARPU, test-market conversion
gaps.whyItMatters: Determines whether consumer AI ever leaves the Unfunded Planned bucket and enters the base case
gaps.resolvedBy: Company disclosure or third-party app-store revenue estimates

gaps.whyItMatters: With no contracts, elasticity is the only defence in a downturn; a spot book with concentrated advertisers is far more fragile than a spot book without

gaps.item: Actual revenue per gigawatt of installed compute
gaps.whyItMatters: The single input that would confirm or destroy the $12.8bn per GW hurdle on which this phase's conclusion rests
gaps.resolvedBy: Meta disclosing fleet GW alongside AI-attributable revenue

risks.text: Zero contracted revenue against a $137bn annual capital programme: advertisers can cut budgets instantly and at no cost, while the capex and lease commitments cannot be cut at all
Incremental operating margin of 3.3% against a 41.4% average means growth is currently diluting returns rather than compounding them
Open-weighting the models forgoes any licensing annuity, so the entire capital programme must be recovered through advertising and first-party products
Youth-safety design mandates cut impressions rather than price - a direct attack on the volume term that has been carrying revenue growth

catalysts.text: First disclosed revenue figure for business messaging, agents or Meta AI subscriptions - would convert the central gap into an underwritable line
Threads and WhatsApp Status ads reach full rollout, revealing whether new inventory is accretive to blended price per ad
Meta AI Plus / Hatch launched beyond test markets at a disclosed price point
A quarter in which incremental operating margin returns above 20%, confirming the capex plateau has begun

conclusions: Meta's contracted revenue is approximately zero. A $137bn annual capital programme is underwritten by a spot auction with no floor, no offtake and no indexation.
Incremental operating margin is 3.3% against an average of 41.4%, computed from management's own expense guidance. Growth dilutes returns.
Free cash flow reaches roughly zero in FY2026 and the dividend is debt-funded: Q2 free cash flow of $784m against $1,353m of dividends.

The required-revenue hurdle is growing as fast as revenue. At a $165-180bn capital run-rate the annual increase in required revenue ($53-58bn) matches or exceeds the actual annual revenue increase ($51-53bn). The base case needs a capex plateau, not a demand surprise.
An independent revenue bridge reproduces the consensus $305bn for FY2027. The disagreement with the market is not about revenue; it is about what the revenue costs.

This demand destroys value at the margin today and relocates value from shareholders to competitive position. It should be underwritten as defensive capex at defensive returns, not as growth capex at growth returns.
thesisImpact: Narrows the investment question to one variable. Demand is real and needs no heroic assumptions; the failure is in converting demand into incremental profit, and it is arithmetically attributable to the capital programme rather than to competition, regulation or user decline. Everything else in this company is working. The question Phase 4 must stress and Phase 5 must price is: when does capex plateau?
